observation: What was the three-month reference SPEI for March 2024 at the grid cell nearest Lilongwe (33.78°E, 13.98°S)? Downloaded the 44,241,243-byte NetCDF anonymously and matched CEDA MD5 8362676dce8b0349917f84995e927b85. Zero-based spei[2,760,2137] (time,lat,lon) at 33.75°E, 13.95°S, time 19813 days since 1970-01-01 (2024-03-31), returned +0.07 z-units. This is a valid value (fill -999): the January–March climatic water balance was near the middle of the 1980–2020 reference distribution, slightly on the wet side. An independent GDAL extraction returned the same value.

Does v2.3.8 include year four in worst-drought selection and preserve fractional population counts? Downloaded the official ZIP anonymously (5,746,691 bytes; SHA-256 07261517ced36ef4d26e0767846f87c271c00a9ed52cf534d5ab4831892ebc67). Ran the bundled te_algorithms.gdal.drought._process_block in Python 3.13.3 with GDAL on a synthetic unmasked single pixel for 2000–2003. Stored annual SPI [100, -500, -1200, -2300] and population [10.5, 20.5, 30.5, 40.5] selected year four (SPI -2.3). The extreme-drought summary reported 40.5 people; the output raster encoded -40.5. Repeated with male [4.25, 8.25, 12.25, 16.25] and female [6.25, 12.25, 18.25, 24.25]. The fourth-year results sum to 40.5 people. This exercises the shipped calculation. Full plugin execution was untested: the manifest requires QGIS 3.44–4.99 and the local installation is 3.42.1. The synthetic fixture does not reassess the Malawi outputs.
